record_type_quote: We attempted to replicate a brief social–psychological intervention reported in Cohen et al. (2006) that has been replicated with varying degrees of success by others. In neither of the two schools did our version of the affirmation intervention appear to boost performance as we had hoped.

targets.authors: Sherman, D. K., Hartson, K. A., Binning, K. R., Purdie-Vaughns, V., Garcia, J., Taborsky-Barba, S., . . . Cohen, G. L.
targets.title: Deflecting the trajectory and changing the narrative: How self-affirmation affects academic performance and motivation under identity threat.
targets.evidence_quote: We also explored whether affirmations worked best for the lowest performing students, as has been found in prior research (Sherman et al., 2013).
targets.outcome_quote: We also explored whether affirmations worked best for the lowest performing students, as has been found in prior research (Sherman et al., 2013). To pursue this possibility, we included the students’ previous term GPA as a covariate and interaction term with experimental condition and ethnic stereotype status. This controls for prior differences in achievement and allows an even more powerful test of the effect. In this model, previous term GPA significantly predicted later term GPA (b ¼ .952, 95% confidence interval [CI] [0.879, 1.024]), no other main effect or interaction approached significance (all ps > .266).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The reported test does not support the corresponding original finding.

reasoning: New students in two schools test Cohen et al. (2006) Study 1. An additional explicit exploratory test checks Sherman et al. (2013)’s low-achiever moderation finding; it is separately included. Cohen 2009 and other intervention papers describe follow-up/background rather than distinct findings this paper tests.
